# Registered website captures

These are real Chromium screenshots taken on 2026-11-10 in new, unauthenticated browser
contexts. They are development/regression data, not held-out generalisation evidence or proof
that the game plugin can operate a browser. No site source code or account state is bundled.
Images retain the sites' visible artwork and attribution; copyright remains with their owners.

- [2048 AI](https://ovolve.github.io/2048-AI/), profile `ovolve_2048`, viewport 1280×1000,
  device scale factor 1. The site's **Auto-run** and **Get Hint** controls were not used.
  [ovolve.json](ovolve.json) records the visible tile DOM independently of the pixel reader for
  the initial/progress answers. The full terminal board was transcribed from its visible numerals;
  it is recognisably terminal by the game rules before the delayed overlay appears. A second
  terminal capture includes the overlay: profile revision 2 reads it as the end screen (`over`)
  covering the board, so the tiles behind it stay unread. Until revision 6 its anchors sat on the score box, outside
  the overlay; the `won` overlay colour is derived from the site's stylesheet (`rgba(237,194,46,.5)`
  over the board colour), not from a capture. The manifests record the browser
  version, exact URLs, capture times, PNG digests and the collection key sequences. Initial random
  spawns were not overwritten, so a new collection is not expected to produce identical boards.
- [Block Blast](https://blockblast.org/), profile `blockblast_org`, viewport 1280×900,
  device scale factor 1. The page loads a Unity canvas using
  `https://appleworm.io/game/block-blast/Build/block-blast.loader.js`. A fresh context's **Play**
  control and three tutorial placements lead to the normal board. [blockblast.json](blockblast.json)
  contains independent visual annotations: an empty 8×8 board with 2×3, 3×3 and 2×2 tray pieces;
  then the first piece at the board's top left, with that slot consumed. The held-drag, tutorial
  and loading captures are rejection/unknown cases. No reader output was used to label them.
  Collection used ordinary pointer events; no localStorage, game memory, DOM or renderer was
  modified to create a board. The collection gestures are not the plugin's input path.

The nine PNGs are unaltered full-viewport captures. Auxiliary advertisements are outside the
profile's reading regions. Expected state is authored separately, not generated by the reader;
tests additionally alter images in memory to cover occlusion, an unknown piece colour, a stray
pixel, a shifted tile and geometry changes. Those alterations are synthetic faults and are not
additional live-site observations.

## Supported reading scope

The two profiles explicitly support the captured desktop layouts in their playing appearance.
Site URLs are provenance only: loading a profile does not route tasks or grant input permission.
The 2048 reader samples tile backgrounds away from digits and gutters. The block reader maps
several registered colours to occupancy; its tray reader finds solid tile interiors and checks
their lattice plus all background outside the inferred tile footprints. A consumed slot must
match its entire registered background. An unknown piece stays `[]`, not `null`.

Score remains unknown. Loading, tutorial and unsettled input are refused or remain unknown; the profiles do not parse arbitrary overlays, terminal messages or new skins.
Profiles register no pixel positions: the board is measured on a capture from the profile's frame
colour and everything else is placed relative to it (plan §4.4). Each manifest names the capture its
cases' board is measured on (`measured_on`, overridable per case): a session measures its board once
and reads its later screens, including end screens and held pieces that no board can be measured on,
with that geometry. Every playing capture must also measure its own board to the same rectangle.
Reading these few examples does not establish all states, colours, pieces or window sizes on either site.

There is no automatic collector in the test suite: focused tests are offline and use no paid
model, browser or network. To refresh a fixture, open the source in a fresh context at the recorded
viewport, collect the screenshot and independent visible-state annotation, record provenance,
inspect it, and only then compare the reader. Never overwrite expected state from its output.
These registered sites and their screenshots must be excluded from the later evaluation of
playing without a pre-registered site profile.

`blockblast_five_cell_tray.png` is a 150×160 tray crop from the 2026-11-11 local
Block Blast run (`blockblast.org`, 1280×900, DPR1), after a real placement refilled the tray.
Its five yellow cells have palette-coloured isolated bevel pixels inside the tile footprints.
The regression distinguishes these from marks outside any proven tile; this crop is reader
coverage, not a separate successful gameplay run.

`blockblast_vertical_tray.png` is a second 150×160 crop from the same local session,
showing five vertical pink cells, the slot box y=700 to 860 of the 1280×900 layout. Its expected
shape is a five-row, one-column piece, independently visible in the crop. Both crops are read with
the background the page's gradient had over those rows, since a crop has no tray band edges.

`blockblast_no_space.png` is an unaltered full-viewport capture (1280×900, DPR1) from the same
2026-11-11 local run (profile revision 3, run 7), taken right after its last placement: the game's
"No Space Left" banner covers the tray while the board stays visible. The board was transcribed
cell by cell from the image before the reader was run; the tray is expected unread (`[]`) because
the banner covers it, and the scene `over`. Revision 4 of `blockblast_org` samples its scene in the
gap between two tray slots, where the playing background and the banner differ.

`ovolve_glow.png` is the final page of a 2026-11-11 local evaluation run (`tools/evaluate_game_live.py`,
1280×1000, DPR1, Playwright Chromium screenshot), recorded with the page's own tile DOM as the answer.
Tiles of 128 and above cast a glow over nearby board pixels; it tinted the left border where profile
revision 2 sampled its scene, and the run stopped as unreadable mid-game. Revision 3 samples the scene on
the middle of the board's top border, which the end message covers but its text and buttons do not,
and which only a big tile in the middle of the top row can tint.

`ovolve_tinted.png` is the final page of the third 2026-11-11 local evaluation run (same setup as
`ovolve_glow.png`), which stopped as unreadable mid-game. The 256 tile's glow tints the 2 above it a few
levels past the profile's tolerance, toward the colour of a 4; the far side of that cell stays untinted.
The answer is the page's own tile DOM at that moment. Reading the nearest colour by a clear margin reads
it; the strict tolerance left it unknown.

The `play2048_*.png` captures are full-viewport screenshots (1280×1000, DPR1, Playwright
Chromium 156 headless shell) of [the official 2048](https://play2048.co/), profile `play2048_co`, taken on
2026-11-11 in fresh contexts. The board is one `<canvas>` and the page keeps no readable grid, so
[play2048.json](play2048.json) holds answers tracked by the rules instead: from the first screen
(annotated by eye), each key's slide was applied with `slide_merge` and only the one new tile (a 2 or a
4, whose colours were read off the first screens) was taken from the screen; a tile colour seen for the
first time was registered as the value the slide had put there. Every later screen of that 948-move game
agreed with the prediction until the 2048 tile formed. The terminal board, end screen and mid-slide
captures come from a second game played with the baseline policy, read and checked against the rules
after every move. The site's undo, swap and grid power-ups were never pressed.

- Each tile has a vertical colour ramp, steepest at the top: the profile registers the colours seen at
  the rows its samples cover, measured over all 947 settled screens of the first game. A 128's lower
  sample and a 512's upper sample lie only 4 levels apart, so the profile keeps a tolerance of 1; the
  cell's other samples still tell the two apart.
- Tiles of 128 and above glow over the board frame; the frame check reads most of each border, so a
  few tinted samples do not refuse the board.
- The end screens (`over`: "Game Over", Play Again, Undo; `won`: "You Win", Start Over, Keep Going)
  replace the header and move the board 4 px down or 10 px up, so the playing geometry no longer finds
  its frame there: the board is measured again on them, and its tiles (expected grids taken from the
  rules-tracked answers) say what the message would. The win screen appears about a second after the
  2048 tile forms (`play2048_reached_2048.png` is the board before it, with the tile's glow). Their
  "Game Over" and "You Win" are page elements (checked on the live site 2026-11-11) but carry only
  layout classes, no class naming the scene.
- `play2048_initial.png` shows the first-visit welcome popup over the header, not the board.
  `play2048_moving.png` was taken 60 ms after a key: the two sliding tiles leave their cells unread.
  `play2048_over.png` and `play2048_terminal_board.png` showed third-party side advertisements; those two
  boxes (x 30–329 and 950–1249, y 163–762) are painted the page background (250, 248, 240). They lie outside
  every reading region, so the reader sees the captures as taken; all other pixels are unaltered.
- 4096 and larger tiles are not registered: a board holding one stays unread.
- In a 2026-11-11 local evaluation smoke run the profile read the board and planned, but the hostkit
  refused every key: the page holds open author shadow roots (the ad network's reporters and the
  consent wrapper), which its key guard does not accept. The first input observation of a load took
  about 6.5 s while ad frames navigated, hence the profile's 10 s settling timeout.

`blockblast_blue_piece.png` is an unaltered full-viewport capture (1280×900, DPR1) from the 2026-11-11
evaluation smoke run, right after the first-visit tutorial (`tools/game_eval_sites.json`). Its royal-blue
piece was not a registered colour, so revision 4 left the slot unread and the run stopped as unreadable;
revision 5 registers it. The board and tray were annotated from the image.

## Measured geometry captures (2026-11-11, profile revisions 7/5/2)

`blockblast_six_cell.png` is the unaltered final page (1280×900, DPR1) of a 2026-11-11 local evaluation
run (`tools/evaluate_game_live.py`, profile revision 6, game 1). That game, and the next, stopped as
unreadable here: the one-by-six piece in the third slot reaches past that slot's fixed 150 px box. The
board and tray were annotated from the image. The tray is now read from a band and split by background,
so the piece reads.

`blockblast_sized_*.png` are one game captured with Playwright Chromium 156 (headless, DPR1) right after
the first-visit tutorial (`tools/game_eval_sites.json`) at 1280×900, then, with no move in between, after
the window was resized to 1100×780 and to 1440×1000: the game redraws its board at 388 and 498 px in
another place. Each is measured on itself and reads the same annotated state; together they are the
mid-game resize the web adapter must measure again.

`play2048_sized_*.png` are a fresh play2048.co game's first screen (welcome popup over the header) at
1280×1000 and, with no key in between, at 1440×1100, where the board keeps its 480 px and moves. At
1024×800 the board shrinks to 440 px while the page's shadow under it (where the scene is sampled) keeps
its pixel size, so revision 2 refused that size before input; it is not a fixture.

`blockblast_long_piece_over_scene.png` is the unaltered final page (1280×900, DPR1) of the first
measured-geometry smoke run (`tools/evaluate_game_live.py`, 54 moves, 53 confirmed). It stopped as
unreadable because the one-by-six piece in the first slot reached over the scene sample, then between
the first two slots at the height of a one-row piece. Board and tray were annotated from the image.

## No marks beside the board (2026-11-11, profile revisions 8/6/3)

The anchors and the scene sample are gone from every profile: each was a point chosen by hand on one
site at one size, and the game itself covered it (the long piece above) or did not scale it with the
board (play2048.co's shadow at 1024×800). A measured board is confirmed by its own frame around the
cells, most cells in the profile's colours, its cells' samples and the tray; every read checks the
frame again. No pixel marks the scene: `blockblast_no_space.png` reads its board with the whole tray
unread (the banner is wider than any piece, so no slot reads as used) and the end comes from the rules
on the move before it or from a model's look; `ovolve_over.png` leaves its covered board unread from
pixels while its page names the scene; the official 2048's end and win screens are measured again
and judged from their tiles.

## Tatham Mines (`minesweeper`)

[Mines](https://www.chiark.greenend.org.uk/~sgtatham/puzzles/js/mines.html) from Simon Tatham's Portable
Puzzle Collection (MIT), profile `tatham_mines`: ten unaltered full-viewport captures taken on
2026-11-13 in fresh contexts (1280×900, and one at 1100×780, DPR1), with ordinary clicks. The board is a
canvas; the page exposes no grid. Every capture but the first is of a game whose mines were placed by its
game id (`#9x9:x,y,u<mine bitmap>`, the start cell `x,y` opened by the game): [tatham.json](tatham.json)
lists the three layouts, each capture's clicks and the expected grid worked out from the mines by the
rules (each opened cell's count, 0s opening their neighbours), never from a reader. The status bar each
capture showed (`COMPLETED!`, `DEAD!`) is recorded beside it.

The captures cover a random game not started, an opening, numbers alone, every digit from 1 to 8, a won
game (the game then flags every covered cell), a lost one (the mine opened on red; this game shows no other
mine), the board elsewhere in a smaller window, and the flash a win or a loss starts with, which no
reader may take for a board: the win's flash reads unknown, and the loss's reads as every cell a mine
opened, which the rules refuse. The board's frame is sunk: grey on its top and left, white on its right
and bottom (`board.frame.opposite`).
